messages:
Priyanka M (AE): DataHarbor POC execs emailed asking for an assurance bundle today: SOC 2 report excerpt, ISO cert, pen-test attestation, list of subprocessors, and a short doc mapping our SOC control IDs to the customer questionnaire they attached. They also asked whether Dedicated vs Private affects data residency guarantees and pricing. Need a tight reply by COB.

Samir G (Solutions): I can assemble the bundle. For the SOC control mapping, please attach the customer's questionnaire (they sent a 12-row spreadsheet). I usually create a 1-page mapping: our SOC control ID -> short description -> pointer to SOC/ISO page.

Jordan L (Security): We have a standard pen-test attestation template and a subprocessors list (current as of last month). Note: subprocessors list includes cloud provider infra, third-party monitoring, and analytics vendor; we can produce a redacted list if they need limited visibility. For pen-test attestation we require the exact recipient "TO:" line and an accept-our-template ack. Turnaround ~48 hours after recipient confirmed.

Elena R (Infra Ops): Quick on Residency: Hosted (standard API) stores data in multi-region infra; we have EU region options for data-at-rest residency but not full private tenancy. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools within a customer VLAN and stronger tenancy isolation; Private (VPC / on-prem) is the only option to guarantee exclusive physical tenancy and full control over residency. Pricing impacts: Dedicated = baseline uplift + setup; Private = custom pricing (licensing + infra + integration). Ballpark: Dedicated uplift for small pool ~ $8k/mo + $4k one-time; Private starts at ~$40k/mo (very rough) and requires longer lead time (multi-week).

Mark D (Legal): For subprocessors we can provide the standard list and a checkbox doc that confirms we flow down appropriate security obligations. If they require a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with specific subprocessor clauses we can route to contracts. For the pen-test letter: Legal signs as 'Redwood Inference, Inc. Legal Counsel (on behalf of Security)'. Need recipient legal entity name and email.

Priyanka M (AE): Attached questionnaire from DataHarbor: https://files.dataharbor/qna-rows.csv — can someone make the 1-pager mapping and upload the bundle to the Assurance dataroom? I'll tell them signed pen-test in ~48h after they confirm "TO:" and whether they want Dedicated or Private pricing.

OpsBot: Assurance dataroom created: https://dataroom.redwood/assurance/DATAHARBOR-5932104321 (view-only).

Samir G (Solutions): Will generate SOC->questionnaire mapping and sanitized subprocessors list. Uploading SOC-excerpt.pdf, ISO27001-cert.pdf, subprocessors-current.csv (redacted), soc-mapping.pdf, pen-test-template.docx (unsigned) to dataroom now. ETA 30m.

Jordan L (Security): Note re: subprocessors: if they need an expanded disclosure we can request approvals from the vendors; that adds 3-5 business days. Also we won't include raw scan logs in the pen-test attestation.

Elena R (Infra Ops): Clarifying residency bullets for reply (copy/paste): 
- Hosted API: multi-region, EU data residency available in EU region (logical residency), standard shared tenancy.
- Dedicated: isolated GPU pool, customer VLAN, stronger tenancy isolation; logical residency in chosen region; provisioning ETA ~7-10 business days after PO. Estimated uplift: ~$8,000/mo + ~$4,000 one-time.
- Private: customer-dedicated control plane (VPC or on-prem), full residency controls, custom pricing & timeline (usually multiple weeks).

Mark D (Legal): I'll prepare a short subprocessor attestation (we confirm flow-down of SOC-level obligations) and the letter template for pen-test signing once they provide recipient. I need their legal entity exact string.

Priyanka M (AE): Thanks team. I'll message DataHarbor now with the dataroom link, tell them we uploaded drafts, ask for the exact "TO:" line for the pen-test letter, whether they want Dedicated pricing or a Private proposal, and whether they accept our subprocessors redaction policy. Will update here when they reply. :pray:
